Without parentheses, JSX that spans several lines has to start on the same line as the `return` or the `=`, so its opening tag does not line up with its closing tag. If you move it down a line, `return` followed by a line break returns `undefined`. With parentheses the JSX can start on its own line.

JSX on one line never needs parentheses.

`--fix` adds the parentheses, or removes them with `"never"`.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}
```jsx
function Card({ title }) {
  return <section>
    <h2>{title}</h2>
  </section>;
}
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```jsx
function Card({ title }) {
  return (
    <section>
      <h2>{title}</h2>
    </section>
  );
}

const empty = <section />;
```

## Options

Each option is a place where JSX can appear:

| Option | Default | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `declaration` | `"parens"` | `const card = <section>` |
| `assignment` | `"parens"` | `card = <section>` |
| `return` | `"parens"` | `return <section>` |
| `arrow` | `"parens"` | `() => <section>` |
| `condition` | `"ignore"` | The branches of `open ? <section> : null` |
| `logical` | `"ignore"` | The right side of `&&`, `\|\|` and `??` |
| `prop` | `"ignore"` | `<Page header={<section>} />` |

Each takes one of these values:

| Value | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `"parens"` or `true` | Require parentheses. |
| `"parens-new-line"` | Require parentheses, with `(` and `)` on other lines than the JSX. |
| `"never"` | Report parentheses around the JSX, even on one line. |
| `"ignore"` or `false` | Do not check this place. |

{/* bad {"options": [{"declaration": "parens-new-line"}]} */}
```jsx
const card = (<section>
  <h2>{title}</h2>
</section>);
```

{/* good {"options": [{"declaration": "parens-new-line"}]} */}
```jsx
const card = (
  <section>
    <h2>{title}</h2>
  </section>
);
```

{/* bad {"options": [{"logical": "parens"}]} */}
```jsx
const panel = (
  <main>
    {open && <section>
      <h2>{title}</h2>
    </section>}
  </main>
);
```

{/* bad {"options": [{"return": "never", "declaration": "never"}], "count": 2} */}
```jsx
function Card({ title }) {
  return (
    <section>
      <h2>{title}</h2>
    </section>
  );
}

const empty = (<section />);
```

While `condition` is `"ignore"`, the branches of a conditional that is declared or assigned are checked under `declaration` or `assignment`:

{/* bad */}
```jsx
const card = open ? <section>
  <h2>{title}</h2>
</section> : null;
```

## When not to use it

A formatter such as `bun format` or Prettier already adds these parentheses.
